stories.headline: BRO says excavator work near Sheshnag lake is post-Amarnath Yatra track widening
stories.dek: Congress, CPM, PDP and Hurriyat leaders demanded the work stop after a video showed an excavator near the glacial lake in Anantnag district.
stories.summary: The Border Roads Organisation said on Monday that it is widening existing tracks near Sheshnag lake after the Amarnath Yatra, following a viral video of an excavator at the site. Opposition and J&K leaders called for the work to stop, citing risks to the glacial lake.
body: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) said on Monday that it is carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works near Sheshnag lake in Anantnag district, after a video of an excavator at the high-altitude site drew criticism from political leaders.

In a statement, the BRO, which comes under the Ministry of Defence, said the works comply with "all the applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards". It said it takes measures to ensure safe disposal of excavated material, protect natural drainage and minimise disturbance to surrounding terrain.

The BRO called the circulating video's claim of new works incorrect. It said that, based on experience of the previous yatra and a requirement for a wider road, it has started widening tracks and stabilising vulnerable stretches to ease congestion and allow safer passage. The works are confined to existing tracks, it said.
The Indian Express reported that the BRO did not explain why earth movers are being used in the high mountains despite the concerns raised.

The video was first shared by an Instagram account, 'Neeraj_excavator_lover', and later deleted by the user. It showed an excavator being used to create a road near the lake, which lies on the trekking route from Pahalgam to the Amarnath cave shrine.

Congress MP Pawan Khera said Sheshnag is among 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified in Jammu & Kashmir. "Sheshnag is not a construction site," he said, describing it as a fragile ecosystem and a lake sacred to both Hindus and Muslims.

CPM legislator M Y Tarigami said the lake is surrounded by loose moraine and steep slopes, and that heavy machinery there is "an invitation to disaster". He said he was not opposed to development but wanted scientific studies, environmental impact assessments and consultations. He asked for details of the project, the agency and the clearances, and for glaciologists to inspect the site. He also said the risks extend downstream to Pahalgam and areas along the Lidder.

Former MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said Kashmir's mountains are "not BJP's real estate". PDP's Muntazir Mehdi said any careless intervention could affect the lake, its catchment and downstream water systems. PDP leader Mohit Bhan called the work a "crime against Hindu faith", according to The Indian Express.
Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said the mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection and that the work "must be immediately stopped".

stories.headline: Mexico captures FBI most-wanted drug lord with US drone and intelligence support
stories.dek: President Claudia Sheinbaum said US forces did not operate on the ground, and a Mexican official said Fausto Isidro Meza Flores will be tried in Mexico.
stories.summary: Mexican forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', in Sinaloa after the US flew a surveillance drone and shared intelligence, officials said. Twenty people died in the fighting that followed.
body: Mexican forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro" and listed among the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives, in Sinaloa state, with US intelligence and a US surveillance drone helping to locate him, Mexican officials said on Monday.

Elite Mexican units detained Meza Flores on Saturday after heavy gunfire around his compound in the Guasave area, according to Bloomberg. Defence Secretary Gen. Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said 16 members of his group were captured with him and 16 alleged associates were killed.

Four soldiers also died, and ten federal agents were injured, Trevilla said. Officials had first reported seven suspected gang members dead before more bodies were found. The Associated Press, cited by France 24, reported 20 deaths in Guasave: four soldiers and 16 suspected criminals. The operation involved hundreds of troops, special forces and several Black Hawk helicopters.

Trevilla said the arrest followed "very important intelligence sharing" with US authorities over three months to pinpoint Meza Flores' location. In the week before the capture, Mexico authorised the US to fly intelligence drones over its territory, he and other officials said. They said the mission complied with Mexican law.

At her regular morning press conference, President Claudia Sheinbaum said the operation was planned and led by Mexican forces, with no US agents on the ground. "The areas in which we coordinate with the US are security and intelligence. That was the agreement we reached from the start," she said. "But they do not conduct operations in Mexico." She confirmed Mexico had asked the US to deploy a drone but gave no further details.
The US government highlighted its intelligence support but did not immediately give details on the drone when asked. US Ambassador Ronald Johnson pointed to intelligence sharing in a post on X.
Authorities noted that the US has an extradition request for Meza Flores on drug trafficking charges. ThePrint reported, citing an official, that he will be tried in Mexico.

The US had offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest or conviction. The US Treasury Department says his group, the Guasave Cartel, has trafficked drugs into the US since at least 2000. It has been fighting a turf war against a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. Under Meza Flores, the group was allied with the faction led by the family of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada.

Experts cited by AP said that removing cartel leaders without dismantling the surrounding structures has often led to violent power struggles between factions, as has happened in Sinaloa in recent years.
keyFacts: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was arrested in Sinaloa on Saturday.
Mexican officials say 16 associates were killed and 16 detained; four soldiers died.
Mexico authorised US intelligence drone flights in the week before the arrest.
The US had offered a $5 million reward for information on Meza Flores.
A Mexican official said he will be tried in Mexico, despite a US extradition request.
stories.background:
Meza Flores led the Beltran Leyva organisation before heading his own group. The arrest follows the February death of Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera, who died of injuries while being taken to hospital after a military raid.

US President Donald Trump has pressed Sheinbaum for two years to act more aggressively against cartels. After meeting her in China last week, he repeated that the cartels are "running Mexico", a claim she rejects.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows deeper US-Mexico security cooperation while Mexico maintains that US forces may not operate on its soil. Whether Meza Flores is tried in Mexico or extradited will be watched by both governments.

stories.headline: 24 killed in fire at candy factory in Serang, Indonesia
stories.dek: Firefighters were still cooling debris on Monday, two days after the blaze began, over fears that fires could reignite at the two-storey building.
stories.summary: A fire that began on Saturday afternoon at a candy factory in Serang, Banten Province, killed 24 people, police said. Hundreds of people were in the compound, and family members have given DNA samples to help identify remains.
body: A fire at a candy factory in Serang, in Indonesia's Banten Province, has killed 24 people, police said on Monday. The blaze began on Saturday afternoon and burned for hours.

Two days later, firefighters were still cooling charred debris in the two-storey building, out of concern that fires might flare up again. Serang is about 50 kilometres, or 30 miles, from the capital, Jakarta.

The factory is owned by Fonusa Agung Mulia and makes milk candies and lollipops sold under the Milkita brand. The company said 300 people were inside the compound on Saturday. About 65 of them were believed to be in the area where the fire started.
Rescue workers in masks carried black body bags out of the wrecked structure, whose roof had partly collapsed. Bags containing human remains were sent to hospitals for identification.
Police said on Monday that dozens of family members had provided DNA samples. Said Iqbal, an adviser to President Prabowo Subianto, visited the site.
The sources available did not state the cause of the fire.

The fire began on Saturday afternoon at a factory in Serang, Banten Province.
The company said 300 people were in the compound, about 65 near the fire's origin.
The factory, owned by Fonusa Agung Mulia, makes Milkita candies and lollipops.
Dozens of relatives have given DNA samples for identification.

stories.headline: Drone attack in Colombian city of Cúcuta injures three, including an infant
stories.dek: Officials say explosive drones hit a home in the first such strike inside a major Colombian population centre, as armed groups target security forces.
stories.summary: Explosive drones destroyed a home in Cúcuta, Colombia, on Monday and injured three people, including an infant, in what a security adviser described as the first such attack in a major city. The United Nations has reported a 445 percent rise in drone bombings.
body: Drones carrying explosives destroyed a home in the Colombian city of Cúcuta on Monday and injured three people, including an infant, in the first such attack inside a major population centre, according to a regional security adviser and news reports.

George Quintero, a retired colonel who advises the regional government on security, said the attack took place at about 3 a.m. He told Colombian radio the drones were most likely launched by one of two armed groups fighting for control of illicit economies. The New York Times reported his account. Al Jazeera described the target as a police base and reported that an infant was among the injured.

Until now, drone strikes in Colombia have mostly occurred in relatively rural areas, the New York Times reported. In the past two years, commercially available drones fitted with explosives have given armed groups new ways to attack government forces and frighten civilians.
The United Nations has reported a 445 percent increase in drone bombings in the country, the New York Times said.

The Wall Street Journal reported that insurgents are using homemade rockets and drones against police and military installations, challenging President de la Espriella's pledge to crush criminal networks. Al Jazeera said the president, whom it described as far-right, has stepped up an offensive and that rebel groups have responded with drone strikes and roadside bombs.
The Colombian military has long fought armed insurgencies and criminal groups with financial and technical help from the United States, according to the New York Times.
keyFacts: Attack on Cúcuta occurred at about 3 a.m. on Monday, according to George Quintero.
Three people were injured, including an infant, per Al Jazeera.
The UN has reported a 445 percent rise in drone bombings in Colombia.
Armed groups use drones and homemade rockets against police and military sites, the Wall Street Journal said.
stories.background: Colombia's military has fought insurgents and criminal groups for decades, with financial and technical help from the United States. In the last two years, cheap commercial drones fitted with explosives have become a tool for armed groups, mainly in rural areas.
stories.whyItMatters: The strike brings a tactic previously seen in rural areas into a major city, putting civilians in urban areas within reach of armed groups' drones.

stories.headline: HAL commits to deliver 16 to 18 Tejas Mk-1A jets to IAF by March 31, 2027
stories.dek: The Air Force will accept the aircraft without relaxing capability requirements, officials said, as deliveries run nearly two years behind schedule.
stories.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd has told the Indian Air Force it will deliver a squadron's worth of Tejas LCA Mk-1A jets, 16 to 18 aircraft, by March 31, 2027, officials said. The first deliveries are nearly two years late.
body: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) has committed to delivering 16 to 18 Tejas LCA Mk-1A fighters to the Indian Air Force (IAF) by March 31, 2027, officials familiar with the discussions said on Monday.

The assurance was given at a review meeting at Air Headquarters on November 16, according to Hindustan Times. Those present included Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, the IAF chief, and Ravi K, HAL's chairman and managing director.

One official, who asked not to be named, said all hardware-related issues, including those linked to weapons trials, have been resolved. "Remaining software-related issues, including those concerning the radar, are in the final stages of resolution," the official said.
The IAF will take the aircraft without granting concessions on capability requirements, the report said. An HAL official said the company is also not seeking any concessions.

HAL will begin the documentation process at the same time. It will approach the Bengaluru-based Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification (CEMILAC) for the release to service document, and seek a signal-out certificate from the Directorate General of Aeronautical Quality Assurance. These documents authorise the user to operate a new air system within specified conditions and approved flight envelopes.
The IAF placed two orders with HAL for 180 Mk-1A jets worth a combined ₹1.1 lakh crore. The first, for 83 aircraft, was signed in February 2021, and the second, for 97, in September 2025.

Deliveries under the first order were due to start in March 2024. That date was missed because of several factors, including GE Aerospace's inability to supply F404-IN20 engines on time and delays in securing key certifications. HAL now aims to execute the 2021 order in three to four years. Deliveries under the second contract are expected to begin in 2027-28 and conclude in six years.

The IAF operates 29 fighter squadrons against an authorised 42.5. It currently flies 38 LCA Mk-1 aircraft. The Mk-1A is meant to replace the MiG-21s, which retired last year after more than six decades of service.

Dixit took over as chief on October 31 and has named the Mk-1A, the LCA Mk-2 and the advanced medium combat aircraft programmes as top priorities. HAL has joined the front, centre and rear fuselage sections of the Mk-2 and is targeting a first ground run by March 2027, with a maiden flight later that year. The IAF will now move a case for Mk-2 procurement.
keyFacts: HAL committed to deliver 16 to 18 Tejas Mk-1A jets by March 31, 2027.
The review meeting at Air Headquarters took place on November 16.
The IAF ordered 180 Mk-1A jets in two contracts worth ₹1.1 lakh crore.
The IAF has 29 fighter squadrons against an authorised 42.5.
HAL targets the first ground run of the LCA Mk-2 by March 2027.
stories.background: The first Mk-1A order, signed in February 2021, called for deliveries to begin in March 2024. Late engine supply from GE Aerospace and delays in certification pushed the schedule back by nearly two years.
stories.whyItMatters: The IAF is short of fighter squadrons, and the Mk-1A is intended to replace the retired MiG-21s and rebuild its strength.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in $43.9 billion all-stock deal
stories.dek: CEO George Kurtz defended the acquisition on Monday as CrowdStrike shares fell about 9% and Zscaler shares rose nearly 18%.
stories.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion in stock, its largest deal to date. CEO George Kurtz defended the purchase as investors worried about dilution, saying it would be accretive to free cash flow per share after closing.
body: CrowdStrike said on Monday it will buy network security firm Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal, the largest acquisition in the Austin, Texas-based company's history.

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, according to CNBC. The deal is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028.

CrowdStrike shares fell about 9% on Monday, with investors raising concerns about dilution because the company will issue new shares to fund the purchase. Zscaler shares rose between 17% and nearly 18%, according to CNBC's reports.

Speaking to CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money", Kurtz rejected the dilution concern. "On a free cash flow per share basis, it's immediately accretive right after close," he said. He added that even with modest synergies the deal would add to revenue, operating margin and free cash flow margin.

Kurtz said the deal expands CrowdStrike's addressable market by roughly $185 billion. He said the two companies share only about 2,000 accounts, leaving roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers that do not use CrowdStrike. "There's very little overlap," he said.

In a statement, Kurtz said the combination would build "a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely." He described Zscaler as CrowdStrike's "No. 1 technology partner" and pointed to a relationship dating back to at least 2019.

Zscaler, based in San Jose, California, provides cloud security and zero-trust products to about 8,000 enterprise customers, according to TechCrunch. CrowdStrike's Falcon platform protects devices and cloud systems. Zscaler adds security across the networks that connect them.

Zscaler CEO and founder Jay Chaudhry told "Mad Money" that bringing the platforms together would make the companies the best protection against AI attacks. He said, "we're coming from strength, both of us."

CrowdStrike also reported fiscal third-quarter earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue, above the LSEG forecast of 31 cents on $1.53 billion. The company had been due to report on December 1 and moved the release forward to coincide with the announcement. Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter results, also released Monday, beat estimates.
As of Friday's close, the two companies had a combined market value above $265 billion, behind Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.
keyFacts: CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal.
Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

stories.background: Cybersecurity deal-making has been active this year. Google announced plans last year to buy Wiz for $32 billion, and Cisco paid about $28 billion for Splunk in 2024. Palo Alto Networks closed a $25 billion deal for CyberArk earlier this year. CNBC reported that recent hacks and outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration and JPMorgan Chase have heightened concern about vulnerabilities in corporate systems.
stories.whyItMatters: The deal would unite device and network security under one company, affecting about 8,000 Zscaler enterprise customers. It would also narrow CrowdStrike's gap with market leader Palo Alto Networks.

stories.headline: Namma Metro ridership rises 12.29% in 2025–26; fare revenue up 49.36%
stories.dek: BMRCL's annual report puts fare-box collections at ₹1,125.58 crore, while residents near Kengeri have petitioned for a Kaniminike station on the proposed Bidadi extension.
stories.summary: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited reported 310.49 million passenger journeys in 2025–26, up 12.29%, and fare-box revenue of ₹1,125.58 crore. Separately, Kaniminike residents have petitioned BMRCL for a station on the proposed Challaghatta–Bidadi extension.
body: Namma Metro recorded 310.49 million passenger journeys in the financial year 2025–26, a 12.29% increase over the previous year, and fare-box revenue rose 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore, according to the annual report of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL).
The previous year's figures were 276.51 million journeys and ₹753.59 crore in fare revenue. Average daily ridership rose to 8.51 lakh passengers from 7.57 lakh, an increase of 12.42%.
The highest single-day ridership was 10.82 lakh passengers on August 14, 2025. Fare-box revenue that day was ₹4.58 crore, a single-day record for the corporation.
BMRCL attributed the growth in fare collections mainly to higher ridership after the 19.15-km Reach-5 Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra was commissioned in August 2025.

Non-fare revenue rose 61.02% to ₹88.51 crore from ₹54.97 crore. The corporation earns it from leasing station spaces, advertising, parking, and electric vehicle charging and battery-swapping stations.

The report put operational profit at ₹417.42 crore and cash profit at ₹209.66 crore. Expenditure, excluding depreciation and finance costs, was ₹823.69 crore. Trains ran with 99.85% punctuality, it said.
The report also cited tokens, Smart Cards, QR tickets and National Common Mobility Cards for improving convenience and cutting transaction time at stations.

Separately, residents of Kaniminike and nearby villages near Kengeri have signed a petition asking BMRCL to include a station at Kaniminike on the proposed Challaghatta–Bidadi extension of the Purple Line, according to The Times of India. They wrote to the BMRCL managing director.

Residents said the BDA Kaniminike housing project has about 1,500 occupied units, with another 1,500 coming up. They also cited nearby colleges and industries in Kumbalagodu and the Bidadi belt, and a proposed South Western Railway halt at Kaniminike that could make the site a multimodal interchange.
Petition initiator Shashank B said the extension is at the feasibility stage and that a station would "improve public transport connectivity and support the region's growing residential activity."
keyFacts: BMRCL logged 310.49 million passenger journeys in 2025–26, against 276.51 million the year before.
Fare-box revenue was ₹1,125.58 crore, up 49.36% from ₹753.59 crore.
Peak ridership of 10.82 lakh came on August 14, 2025.
Operational profit was ₹417.42 crore; cash profit was ₹209.66 crore.
The Challaghatta–Bidadi Purple Line extension is at the feasibility stage.
stories.background: The Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra, a 19.15-km stretch, began operating in August 2025. The Challaghatta–Bidadi extension of the Purple Line is proposed and, according to petitioners, is at the feasibility stage.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show how new lines are affecting Metro use and revenue, while the petition shows residents of growing areas seeking a say in station locations on planned extensions.

stories.headline: BWSSB's service area grows by 2,196 sq km, nearly triple its earlier jurisdiction
stories.dek: The board must now plan water, sewerage and drainage for the added areas while nearly half of the city's 2,580 MLD of sewage is untreated or improperly treated.
stories.summary: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board has added 2,196 sq km to its jurisdiction, nearly three times the roughly 800 sq km it served earlier. It has given no timeline for full coverage of the new areas.
body: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) has added 2,196 sq km of service area to its jurisdiction, nearly three times the roughly 800 sq km it previously served, according to a report in The Times of India.

The expansion widens the board's responsibility for water supply, sewerage and drainage. Its existing jurisdiction covers the core city, the erstwhile seven city municipal councils, one town municipal council and 110 villages.

BWSSB must plan services for the new areas while nearly half of Bengaluru's 2,580 MLD of sewage remains untreated or improperly treated. A master plan will assess current and future populations, topography and geography, and build a GIS-based database of water, sewerage and drainage networks.

The newly merged villages and peripheral layouts need transmission mains, distribution networks, reservoirs, pumping stations and service connections. BWSSB has not given a timeline for full coverage.

Cauvery water travels nearly 140 km and is pumped about 450 metres. BWSSB said demand for Cauvery connections has risen as groundwater levels fell and borewell yields became unreliable. Its Sarala Cauvery initiative offers EMI-based payments for new domestic and non-domestic piped connections.

Cauvery Water Supply Scheme Stage V, recently commissioned, has added 775 MLD and extended services to peripheral areas. Stage VI, expected to add 500 MLD, is at the planning stage. Yettinahole is being considered as a longer-term supplementary source.

BWSSB said continued dependence on Cauvery transfers is unsustainable. About 805 MLD of treated wastewater, roughly 60%, is reused for minor irrigation, lake rejuvenation and industry. The board is also promoting rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and lower distribution losses.

It expects near-complete sewage treatment by 2029 through 45 new sewage treatment plants with a combined capacity of 1,163 MLD. Existing and proposed capacity would total about 2,511.5 MLD, still below present sewage generation of 2,580 MLD.

The board has not disclosed how many plants fail quality standards or run below capacity, or whether contractors face penalties for repeated violations. An independent audit is under way, and the Indian Institute of Science is assessing the quality framework. A real-time dashboard tracks treated water against Karnataka State Pollution Control Board standards, but BWSSB did not say whether plant-wise results would be published. Annual operation and maintenance expenditure is Rs 200 crore.

City demand is 2,650 MLD against supply of 2,720 MLD, including about 800 MLD from borewells. With population projected at around 21 million by 2031 and 28.3 million by 2041, the deficit is expected to reach 575 MLD and 1,670 MLD respectively.

stories.headline: Anthropic mathematician posts Claude-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis
stories.dek: Independent groups say they have verified Levent Alpöge's 250,000-page proof, while a mathematicians' association disputes that anyone can be certain it is correct.
stories.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on November 20, developed over about six weeks with the company's Claude AI. A Lean and Mathlib joint statement backs its correctness; the Association for Human Mathematics disputes this.
body: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic, posted on November 20 a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, saying he developed it over about six weeks with Anthropic's AI tool Claude, according to Science News.

The Riemann hypothesis, dating to 1859, is a statement about prime numbers, the numbers divisible only by themselves and one. It concerns a mathematical function whose "zeros", the inputs that produce an answer of zero, are closely tied to primes. The hypothesis says certain zeros all lie on one line on a graph. If true, it would reveal how many primes exist below a given number.

The proof runs to more than 250,000 pages, Science News and Phys.org reported. Phys.org said the accompanying Lean verification code is over 17 million lines long. Lean is software that turns mathematical arguments into code so a computer can check that each logical step holds. Claude also drew on Mathlib, a library of known results already written in Lean.

The version of Claude Alpöge used has not been disclosed. Alpöge said he has solved not only the Riemann hypothesis but also the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends the idea to related functions.

A joint statement from the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative said: "We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement." Phys.org said independent researchers have verified the Lean proof. Mathematicians are still working to translate the argument into a form people can follow.

Ken Ono of Axiom Math and the University of Virginia said the proof involves so many areas of mathematics that he did not know how one person could hold all the ideas in mind. Bryna Kra of Northwestern University said Alpöge did not simply request a proof and wait. She contrasted it with the OpenAI solution to a Navier-Stokes equations problem, which she said was largely produced by AI agents on their own.

The Association for Human Mathematics said in a November 20 statement that no human can claim responsibility for the proof and that no mathematician can "confirm with full certainty that the proof is correct." Phys.org said the group, whose members commit to AI-free research, has more than 1,000 members.

Gary Marcus of New York University wrote in a Substack post that it is "not at all obvious that whatever Alpöge did has the generality many people are hoping for." He argued that AI's strength in mathematics may not carry over to open-ended problems in biology, business or robotics.
keyFacts: Levent Alpöge posted the proof on November 20, saying he worked with Claude for about six weeks.
The proof runs to more than 250,000 pages; the Lean code exceeds 17 million lines.
Lean Focused Research Organization and Mathlib Initiative said they have full confidence in its correctness.
The Association for Human Mathematics says no one can fully confirm the proof is correct.
The Riemann hypothesis dates to 1859 and concerns the distribution of prime numbers.
stories.background: Phys.org reported that OpenAI and Anthropic models have produced results on many open problems in 2026, including an OpenAI solution to a Navier-Stokes problem and a batch of over 700 papers in October. On September 11, Terence Tao and 25 other Fields medalists issued a declaration saying AI companies' goals and the mathematical community's are "severely misaligned". It has over 8,000 signatures.
stories.whyItMatters: Many mathematical results are conditional on the Riemann hypothesis, so a confirmed proof would affect them. The dispute over verification and authorship bears on how AI-generated mathematics is judged.

stories.headline: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok sexual deepfakes
stories.dek: The attorneys general say X and Grok falsely promoted their safety; X says users deliberately broke its rules and that it screens every request and output.
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia filed separate but similar lawsuits on Monday accusing SpaceX of violating consumer protection laws over sexualised deepfakes made with Grok. X says users deliberately circumvented its safeguards, which it says screen every prompt and output.
body: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed separate but similar lawsuits against SpaceX on Monday, accusing it of violating state consumer protection laws over sexualised deepfakes generated with Grok, the AI chatbot on Elon Musk's X platform.

A deepfake is an image or video altered or generated by artificial intelligence to depict a person doing or appearing in something that did not happen. According to The Verge, the states allege that SpaceX ignored industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoted the safety of X and Grok's AI features. Both suits seek financial damages. Ars Technica reported that the suits also aim to stop Grok from generating child sexual abuse material and revenge porn.

Jones said in a press statement: "Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false." He said the tool allowed users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery, sexualised images and child sexual abuse material.

The Virginia complaint accuses Musk of wilfully ignoring concerns about AI-generated sexualised deepfakes and seeing "a market opportunity for more profits". It describes the weak safeguards as "not a failure but a feature".

The complaints largely concern Grok Imagine, a tool that lets Grok and X users generate images and videos. xAI, which Musk has since merged with SpaceX, launched a "spicy" mode for it in August 2025. The Verge reported that the mode produced sexualised content, including nude deepfakes of celebrities such as Taylor Swift.

In January 2026, Grok gained a feature allowing X users to edit any image without the original poster's consent. The Verge reported that X was then flooded with non-consensual sexualised deepfakes of adults and minors.

xAI later restricted image editing, putting some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear or explicit scenarios. The Verge said its own testing after those changes found they did little to stop the bot creating sexualised deepfakes.

In a statement issued after the lawsuits were announced, the X Safety team said people who tried to use Grok Imagine to make this material did so by deliberately violating its terms of service and working "aggressively to circumvent our safeguards". It said it tightened protections earlier this year and that classifiers, automated systems that sort content, screen every prompt before an image is generated and check every output afterwards.
The states' filings say the safeguards were inadequate; X says they are designed to refuse requests for explicit images of minors or real people. The sources do not give court dates for either case.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix and approve code
stories.dek: Two new agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, are in beta; the approval agent acts on policies a development team writes in plain language.
stories.summary: Anthropic on Monday launched Claude Ship, a set of tools in which Claude reviews, fixes and approves proposed code changes. Two of its three parts are in beta, and the company advises teams to test approvals in observe-only mode first.
body: Anthropic on Monday launched Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents that review proposed code changes, fix problems in them and approve routine ones without a person signing off each time.

The product is available to customers on Claude Team and Enterprise plans whose code is stored on GitHub, a platform where developers keep and share software projects. Anthropic is the newly public AI company behind the Claude chatbot, according to TechCrunch.

Claude Ship has three parts. Code Review, which examines pull requests (proposals to add changes to a codebase), was announced in March and became generally available in October, The Verge reported. The other two agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, entered beta testing on Monday.

PR Steward handles failing CI checks, which are automated tests run on new code, as well as merge conflicts, where two sets of changes clash, and feedback from Code Review, other review tools or team members. After each push of new code, it comments on what it changed and how to roll the change back if needed, TechCrunch reported.

Claude Approvals decides whether a change can be merged into the main codebase. It applies an approval policy that a team writes as a file in its repository, in natural language. Anthropic said the agent can weigh signals including Code Review findings or a team's own classifiers, which are tools that sort changes into categories.
Anthropic said teams keep control over where Claude Ship runs, which review setting to use (Quick, Standard or Deep) and which changes are escalated to a human for a decision.
Because the approval features are in beta, Anthropic suggests running them first in observe-only mode. It also suggests starting with a single repository and setting monthly spending limits.

In a company blog post, Anthropic said: “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now.” It added that on the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of the code, and the company wanted the steps after a pull request to move as fast.
TechCrunch noted that AI coding tools already offered code review, and that the new element is an agent that can approve changes on its own under team-set policies.

stories.headline: Sebi tells market players to stop publishing IPO grey-market premiums
stories.dek: The regulator said unregulated pre-listing figures are unverified and may harm investors, and urged them to avoid transactions linked to such premiums.
stories.summary: Sebi issued an advisory on Monday asking intermediaries and market participants to stop publishing grey market premium figures for IPOs. It said the figures are unofficial and unverified, and that publicising them may be detrimental to investors.
body: The Securities and Exchange Board of India asked intermediaries and market participants on Monday, 23 November, to stop publishing and circulating grey market premium figures for initial public offerings, saying such publicity may harm investors.

In an advisory, the regulator said unregulated pre-listing premiums were being widely disseminated through multiple channels. It noted that some Sebi-registered intermediaries and market participants were among those publishing them.

Sebi described the grey market premium, or GMP, as the unofficial and unverified price at which shares are supposedly traded before they list on a recognised stock exchange. It said publication, display, circulation or dissemination of such premiums, through any mode or platform, may be discontinued across the securities market.

It specifically advised registered intermediaries and market participants not to publish, display or broadcast GMP figures on their websites, platforms or other channels, including emails, SMS and social media.

The regulator said grey market trades take place outside the recognised exchange framework and are not subject to regulatory oversight. Such trades carry no settlement guarantee or investor protection, and follow no formal price-discovery process, it said.

Sebi said circulating the figures could be detrimental to investors' interests and run counter to the principles of transparency and accountability in the securities market. Its concern, as reported by Mint, is that investors may read GMP as a reliable signal of listing price or returns, though no regulated mechanism exists to verify it.

The advisory told investors not to treat grey market premiums as an indicator of likely listing price or expected returns, and to stay away from GMP-linked transactions. Investors should apply for public issues through Sebi-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms, it said.

Sebi also warned that participants in grey market dealings would have no access to formal dispute-resolution routes. These include investor protection under Sebi or stock exchange jurisdiction, exchange-run grievance redressal, and the Online Dispute Resolution portal managed by exchanges and depositories.
keyFacts: Sebi issued the advisory on Monday, 23 November.
It covers Sebi-registered intermediaries and market participants, including on emails, SMS and social media.
Grey market trades carry no settlement guarantees or investor protection, Sebi said.
Grey market participants cannot use the Online Dispute Resolution portal, the regulator said.
stories.background: Grey market premiums are followed by many investors to gauge demand for an upcoming public issue and estimate its likely listing performance. The figures are frequently cited on websites, digital platforms, newspapers and social media.
stories.whyItMatters: Websites, platforms and registered intermediaries that publish GMP figures are being asked to stop, and retail IPO investors are told not to base subscription decisions on them.

stories.headline: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four others flogged over hijab-free concert
stories.dek: Lawyers say a court in Qom enforced 74 lashes each, plus two-year bans on artistic work and foreign travel, over a livestreamed December 2024 performance.
stories.summary: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team were flogged with 74 lashes each in Qom, lawyers and an Iranian news website said on Monday. They were convicted over a concert she performed without a hijab.
body: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her band and production team have each received 74 lashes in the city of Qom, lawyers and an Iranian news website said on Monday.

A member of the defence team told the BBC that Ahmadi and four male co-defendants were flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom. The Emtedad website quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili as confirming the lashes.
The pro-reform daily Etemad, citing Nili, named the four men as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari. Ahmadi is 29.

The case stems from a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024, in which Ahmadi performed in a sleeveless dress without the mandatory hijab, alongside male musicians. Iranian law bans public performances by women and requires them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.

In June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material". The defendants denied the charge. Besides the lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.
An appeals court in Qom rejected their appeal at the end of September and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.

One lawyer told the BBC the defence had sought to overturn or reduce the verdict, or to have it suspended. "The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately," he said.

Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran, called the flogging "a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms".

Western governments and human rights groups have criticised flogging as torture and a violation of international law. Iran rejects accusations over its human rights record and says Western countries should focus on their own problems. When the sentence was issued, other Iranian artists and activists also condemned it.
keyFacts: Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and four others received 74 lashes each in Qom.
The sentence also includes two-year bans on artistic activity and leaving Iran.
The concert was livestreamed in December 2024.
A Qom appeals court confirmed the sentence at the end of September.
stories.background: Hijab rules were a flashpoint in 2022, when protests followed the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman detained for allegedly wearing her hijab improperly. Since then many women have stopped covering their hair in public, and authorities have responded with periodic arrests, warnings and business closures. Reuters and the Guardian report that enforcement has become more selective.
stories.whyItMatters: The flogging shows that courts are still enforcing dress-code and performance bans on women, even as many women in Iran ignore the rules in public.

stories.headline: Magnitude 5.3 earthquake strikes Nepal's Koshi province, felt in eastern India
stories.dek: Agencies gave differing magnitudes for the quake; no casualties or damage had been reported by Tuesday morning, and tremors were also reported in Bhutan, Bangladesh and China.
stories.summary: An earthquake struck Nepal's Koshi province at about 7:02 am IST on Tuesday, with tremors felt in Bihar, West Bengal and Meghalaya. No casualties or damage had been reported, and agencies gave magnitudes between 5.3 and 5.6.
body: An earthquake of magnitude 5.3 struck Nepal's Koshi province at about 7:02 am IST on Tuesday, with tremors reported in parts of eastern and northeastern India, Bhutan, Bangladesh and China, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).

The NCS put the epicentre at latitude 27.855 degrees north and longitude 87.909 degrees east, at a depth of 20 kilometres. It posted on X: "EQ of M: 5.3, On: 24/11/2026 07:02:47 IST, Lat: 27.855 N, Long: 87.909 E, Depth: 20 Km, Location: Nepal." The European Mediterranean Seismological Centre also reported a magnitude of 5.3.

Other agencies differed. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) was cited as placing the quake near Lelep in Koshi province, and Business Standard reported its magnitude as 5.4. Another USGS report, quoted by Mint, said "Magnitude 5.3 earthquake recorded 67 km WNW of Mangan, India."

Nepal's National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Centre put the magnitude at 5.6, with the epicentre near Olangchung Gola in Taplejung district, close to the Nepal-Tibet border, according to The Kathmandu Post as cited by NDTV.

In India, tremors were reported in Bihar, Meghalaya and parts of West Bengal, according to media reports. NDTV reported that the quake shook high-rise buildings, houses, electric poles and overhead power lines in West Bengal, and that residents, including people out on morning walks, ran into the streets. It was felt in North Bengal districts including Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar.
News18, as cited by Mint, reported tremors across several districts of Bihar, with details of affected areas awaited. No casualties or damage had been reported so far.

Separately, the NCS recorded a magnitude 2.5 earthquake in Assam's Karbi Anglong district at 3:39 am on Tuesday, at a depth of 15 kilometres. Its epicentre was at 25.743 degrees north and 93.355 degrees east. Reports did not link the two events.
Outlets said further details on the affected areas were awaited.
keyFacts: The quake struck at about 7:02 am IST on Tuesday, 24 November.
The NCS and EMSC reported magnitude 5.3; Nepal's monitoring centre said 5.6.
The NCS gave a depth of 20 km, with the epicentre in Nepal.
Tremors were reported in Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar in North Bengal.
A separate magnitude 2.5 quake hit Assam's Karbi Anglong at 3:39 am.
stories.background: Nepal's Koshi province borders Tibet and the Indian state of Sikkim. Seismic agencies often report slightly different magnitudes and epicentre locations in the first hours after a quake.
stories.whyItMatters: The tremors were felt across several Indian states and neighbouring countries, prompting residents in North Bengal to leave their homes, though no damage or injuries had been reported.

stories.headline: Nasscom seeks three-year AI transformation scheme for IT firms in Budget
stories.dek: The IT industry body wants the finance and IT ministries to design funding for AI product development, staff retraining and shared infrastructure for smaller firms.
stories.summary: Nasscom has asked the government to commit in Budget 2027-28 to a three-year scheme to help Indian IT firms move to AI-led services. Separately, Tracxn data cited by YourStory shows India AI funding nearly doubled to $1.6B in January-September 2026.
body: Nasscom, the IT industry body, has asked the government to announce a three-year "AI Services Transformation and Innovation Scheme" in the Union Budget 2027-28, saying Indian IT firms need upfront funding to move to AI-led services.

The request is part of the body's pre-Budget submission, made on Monday. Nasscom said generative AI (software that produces text, images or code) and agentic AI (systems that carry out tasks with limited human direction) are changing what clients want, how work is delivered and how IT firms charge for it.

Building AI products and retraining staff requires spending before returns arrive, Nasscom said, and firms must do so while serving existing clients. It said smaller firms are hit hardest because they struggle to fund development, hire specialists and release staff to learn on live projects.

Nasscom proposed that the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Ministry of Finance design the scheme with industry. It would support AI offerings built and run from India that earn revenue through licences, subscriptions, usage-based fees or outcome-linked pricing.

The scheme would also fund supervised, project-based retraining so existing employees can move into new roles and freshers gain practical experience. Smaller firms would get shared technical infrastructure, specialist support and joint projects.

The submission has other asks. For global capability centres (GCCs), the India-based units of multinational companies that handle engineering, research and leadership work, Nasscom wants safeguards against creating a taxable "permanent establishment" for the foreign parent. It said specialist visits of up to 90 days in 12 months, genuine secondments and global roles held by India-based executives should not trigger that status.

On employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs), Nasscom proposed deferring tax on unlisted ESOPs until sale, listing or ten years after exercise, whichever is earlier. It also wants the wage ceiling for additional employment deductions under Section 146 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, raised from ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh a month.

Nasscom also proposed a capped, contributory cybersecurity programme to help small and medium firms put basic protections in place. For restructuring, it sought loss carry-forward benefits for IT and KPO firms undertaking amalgamations, tax neutrality for fast-track demergers, and enforcement of the 10% pre-payment cap for disputed tax stays.
Separately, YourStory reported, citing data from Tracxn, that India's AI funding nearly doubled to $1.6B in January-September 2026. Only the headline of that report was available.
keyFacts: Nasscom made its pre-Budget submission on Monday, November 23.
It proposes a three-year AI Services Transformation and Innovation Scheme in Budget 2027-28.
MeitY and the Finance Ministry would design the scheme with industry.

Tracxn data puts India AI funding at $1.6B for January-September 2026.
stories.background: Nasscom said its tax recommendations build on transfer pricing reforms announced in the previous Budget. Pre-Budget submissions are proposals from industry bodies to the government; they are not commitments.
stories.whyItMatters: If adopted, the scheme would direct public funding to AI product development and retraining, with smaller IT firms, which Nasscom says face the heaviest upfront costs, as intended beneficiaries.

stories.headline: I4C advises against using WhatsApp Web for official or sensitive work
stories.dek: The Home Ministry's cybercrime wing says an active session can be misused and that closing a browser tab does not end it; users must log out manually.
stories.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre issued an advisory on WhatsApp Web, warning that active sessions can be exploited to read messages and impersonate users. It advised against exchanging government or sensitive information on the service and asked users to log out manually after each session.
body: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Union Home Ministry, has advised users to avoid exchanging government, organisational, financial or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web, citing the risk that an authenticated session could be misused.

The advisory was issued on Monday by the I4C's National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU). It said the unit had observed that such a session may, under certain circumstances, be used to gain unauthorised access to a user's WhatsApp account.

According to the advisory, a malicious actor could read messages, send communications while impersonating the account holder, and access contact lists and group conversations. The user's trusted identity could then be used for fraud, phishing and social-engineering attacks.
The unit said closing a browser window or tab is not enough to end an authenticated session. Users should log out manually after each session and should not keep accounts permanently logged in.

It urged particular caution on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices other people can access. It also advised against logging in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed laptops or other unknown computers.

Where WhatsApp Web use is unavoidable, the unit recommended Incognito or Private Browsing mode on a trusted computer, with a manual logout before closing the browser. Institutions and organisations were advised to avoid using WhatsApp Web in official and sensitive work environments.

The advisory asked users to treat unexpected messages sent from their accounts, or unexplained replies from contacts, as serious signs of possible misuse. It also called for updated operating systems, browsers and security software, and for avoiding suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software.

Mint reported that users who suspect a compromise should check the linked devices section in WhatsApp settings and log out of sessions they do not recognise. Cyber fraud can be reported on the national helpline 1930 or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.

stories.whyItMatters: Government employees and other office users who rely on WhatsApp Web on shared computers are advised to change how they handle sensitive information and session logouts.

stories.headline: Pakistani astronaut to fly to Tiangong as first foreigner on Chinese station crew
stories.dek: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former Pakistani armed forces pilot, joins Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi on Shenzhou-24, scheduled to lift off at 8.18am on Wednesday.
stories.summary: China named Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali as part of the Shenzhou-24 crew bound for the Tiangong space station, the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese crewed mission there. Liftoff is scheduled for 8.18am on Wednesday.
body: China will send its first foreign astronaut to the Tiangong space station, with Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali named on Tuesday as part of the Shenzhou-24 crew, which is scheduled to launch at 8.18am on Wednesday.

Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, will fly with Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, according to Zhang Jingbo, spokesman for the China Manned Space Agency and director of its general plan bureau, as reported by the South China Morning Post.

Earlier reports, citing Al Jazeera and Chinese state media, said a Pakistani astronaut had been selected to serve as a payload specialist. Those reports, carried by The Indian Express on Monday, did not name the astronaut or give a departure date.

Ali and fellow Pakistani pilot Khurram Daud were among the candidates who trained for months at the China Astronaut Research and Training Center in Beijing, The Indian Express reported. The training included practical operational exercises and intensive Chinese language instruction.
It followed an agreement signed by Pakistan and China in February 2025 to set up a programme for selecting and preparing Pakistani astronauts for missions to the Chinese station.

Space cooperation between the two countries extends beyond crewed flight. China's National Space Administration is also due to deploy Jinnah-1, Pakistan's first lunar rover. The 35 kg rover carries instruments to study plasma behaviour, radiation levels and the composition of lunar soil.

The Indian Express described the cooperation as part of China's Belt and Road Initiative. It noted that China is Pakistan's largest trading partner and a key foreign investor, and that the two countries have long-standing strategic and diplomatic ties.
NDTV carried a headline quoting a US expert who called the flight a new phase in space diplomacy. The full text of that report was not available.
China has set a target of landing astronauts on the Moon by 2030.

China is also due to deploy Pakistan's Jinnah-1 lunar rover, a 35 kg vehicle carrying scientific instruments.
stories.whyItMatters: The flight is the first time a foreign national will visit China's orbital outpost, extending China-Pakistan cooperation from trade and diplomacy into human spaceflight.

stories.headline: Maiden flight of privately built PSLV-N1 likely pushed to early 2027
stories.dek: The rocket, built by a HAL and L&T consortium, was to carry ISRO's EOS-10 earth observation satellite; at least two launches had been planned this year.
stories.summary: The first flight of the privately built PSLV-N1 is likely to slip to early 2027, The Indian Express reported. An L&T executive cited payload coordination and launch window issues, while sources pointed to ISRO's caution after two PSLV failures.
body: The maiden flight of the privately built PSLV-N1 rocket is likely to be pushed to early 2027, The Indian Express reported on Monday, extending a programme under which at least two launches had been planned this year.
The rocket was to carry ISRO's earth observation satellite EOS-10. It is being built by a consortium led by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Larsen & Toubro (L&T).

A T Ramchandani, Senior Vice-President and Head of L&T Precision Engineering & Systems, said the delays result from issues such as coordination with the payload and the available launch window. He spoke at the India International Space Conclave.

According to the newspaper's sources, the vehicle is ready. They said the present delay stems from ISRO's caution after two successive failures of its PSLV. ISRO will likely clear the privately developed rocket only after its own PSLV flies successfully, the sources said.

One source said that after the setbacks, suppliers of certain components were changed on the recommendation of the failure assessment committee. "The changes have already been made to the PSLVs," the source said.

The two failures were PSLV-C61 on May 18, 2025 and PSLV-C62 on January 12, 2026. Both rockets developed anomalies in the third stage. ISRO maintains the causes were different, and sources said the problems have now been fixed.
The consortium won the contract in 2022 to make five PSLV rockets. The first vehicle was due within two years and the rest every six months, which would have meant delivery of all five by 2026.

Ramchandani also called at the conclave for a Space Components Mission covering space-grade electronics, sensors, propulsion, materials and mechanisms. He said that if India integrates systems domestically but imports radiation-hardened electronics, alloys and sensors, it remains exposed.

Separately, astronaut-designate Air Commodore Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair urged large Indian industrial groups to form a consortium for complex missions, including a human space mission. The first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight is likely later this year, with at least two more flights before a crewed one.

stories.background: The PSLV is ISRO's most used launch vehicle. Four of its flights have failed, including the first in 1993 and one in 2017 when the heat shield did not open. The 2022 contract set a first delivery in 2024.
stories.whyItMatters: The delay extends the timeline for India's first industry-built PSLV, which was meant to shift routine launch manufacturing to private hands under a five-rocket contract.

stories.headline: Storms on both US coasts threaten Thanksgiving travel as king tides flood California
stories.dek: The National Weather Service has warned of heavy rain, coastal flooding and winds that could ground the Macy's parade balloons in New York.
stories.summary: A storm that could intensify rapidly is forecast to hit the US East Coast from Wednesday to Friday, while king tides and a storm bring coastal flood warnings to California. Forecasters say winds could ground the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons.
body: A storm forecast to hit the US East Coast from Wednesday to Friday could disrupt Thanksgiving travel and the Macy's parade in New York, the National Weather Service said, as California separately braces for king tides and more rain.

The weather service said the East Coast storm could bring "bursts of heavy rain and embedded thunderstorms" from Georgia and the Carolinas to southern New England. The Daily Wire reported that the system could rapidly intensify into a bomb cyclone, with coastal flooding and wind gusts of 50 mph or more possible.

Capital Weather, a Washington forecasting service, said 1 to 3 inches of rain and gusts above 40 mph looked possible, and that the rain could challenge the Thanksgiving rainfall record in the US capital.

The Storm Prediction Center has placed South Florida under a risk of severe weather on Wednesday, with damaging winds, isolated tornadoes and flooding rain the main threats. A Miami-based forecaster warned of major airline delays out of Miami and Fort Lauderdale.

New York City safety guidelines bar operating the large parade balloons if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph. This year is the parade's 100th edition. The balloons have been fully grounded by weather once, in 1971, according to The Daily Wire.

In California, a coastal flood warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines runs through Thursday afternoon. The warning cites possible flooding of up to 2.7 feet above ground level in low-lying areas and breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet under a High Surf Warning. It also lists road closures and coastal erosion among expected effects.

NWS Los Angeles advised against visiting beaches, especially on Wednesday and Thursday, and warned of sneaker waves that wash farther up the beach than expected. Los Angeles County expects tides of 8 to 8.9 feet from Monday to Thursday, the New York Post reported.

San Francisco is distributing about 35,000 sandbags and setting up temporary flood barriers. A Tiger Dam temporary flood protection system has been installed near the Bay Bridge, and Oakland International Airport has finished a project to hold back high water. Waymo said it would pause all services across the Bay Area from Monday.

Floodwater surrounded vehicles and a warehouse in Mill Valley on Monday, and residents in Huntington Beach and Long Beach placed sandbags and built sand berms. Last week's storm brought nearly three inches of rain to parts of San Francisco, stalling vehicles, the Post reported.

stories.headline: Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma submits resignation over elephant operation
stories.dek: The Forest Department stopped driving elephants further after 38 entered Mudigere taluk, and Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy has called a meeting on November 30.
stories.summary: Mudigere Congress MLA Nayana Motamma sent her resignation letter to the Speaker's office in Bengaluru on Monday, opposing the Forest Department's drive to move wild elephants. The department has paused the operation, and the Forest Minister will meet legislators and officials on November 30.
body: Mudigere Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation letter to the Speaker's office in Bengaluru on Monday, opposing the Forest Department's operation to drive wild elephants from Hassan towards the Tatkola Reserve Forest in Chikkamagaluru.

The Hindu reported that Congress MLAs from the district had threatened to resign over the drive. Residents of Mudigere and neighbouring taluks have said they are worried, and many gathered in Mudigere town on Monday to urge the state government to withdraw the elephants from the taluk and ensure people's safety.
M.K. Pranesh, a former MLC, said the taluk would call a Mudigere bandh if the government did not respond to the people's demands.

The department stopped driving the animals further after 38 elephants entered Mudigere taluk, acting on instructions from senior officers. Chikkamagaluru Deputy Conservator of Forests K.T. Boraiah said on Monday that no drive would be carried out that day. He said there would be no driving for now, as the coffee harvest is under way in the region.

The elephants have split into two groups about 2-3 km apart, one at Baradahalli and the other at Makonahalli. Between 60 and 70 personnel have been deployed, and drones are tracking the herds. Schools in nearby areas have been given a holiday as a precaution.

Boraiah asked the public, especially planters, not to burst crackers or send workers near the animals. He also urged people not to go out of curiosity or shoot videos for social media. "Everybody's life is important, and we need the public's cooperation," he said.

Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy has convened a meeting of elected representatives and senior forest officials in Bengaluru on November 30. It will discuss the movement of the herds, public safety and measures to prevent repeated human-elephant conflict.

Wild elephants have been reported in parts of Hassan since the 1980s, spreading from Sakleshpur to Alur and Belur taluks. According to earlier reports cited by The Hindu, 24 people have died in elephant attacks in Hassan district since 2020-21.

The deaths of two people in Belur taluk within three days last week led the department to launch the drive. Officials captured two tuskers said to be responsible and shifted them to Nagarahole. They then began moving the herds towards the 874-hectare Tatkola Reserve Forest.

stories.headline: Gill blames Wellington pitch for draw as NZ's Tickner is ruled out of second Test
stories.dek: India stay fourth in the World Test Championship table after the first Test ended drawn, and New Zealand replace the injured seamer with Matt Fisher.
stories.summary: India captain Shubman Gill called the Basin Reserve surface "not a great Test wicket" after the first Test against New Zealand ended in a draw. New Zealand Cricket said seamer Blair Tickner will miss the second Test with a hamstring injury.
body: India captain Shubman Gill said the Basin Reserve pitch became too flat and slow to produce a result, after the first Test against New Zealand ended in a draw in Wellington on Monday.

"On Day(s) 3, 4, and 5, it just went flatter and flatter," Gill said. "There were no indentations on the wicket... I think it was not a great Test wicket, especially if you want results." According to The Indian Express, more than 1,300 runs were scored for 24 wickets over the five days.

India declared on 720-9 in their only innings, Sportstar reported. Former India off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin said that on the final day India took five wickets and that New Zealand had not crossed the deficit when the draw was accepted with 15 overs left.

Ashwin said on his YouTube channel that he wanted to see the last 15 overs played. "Why not? Because since you have taken five wickets, why can't you try a bit more?" he said. He also criticised the lack of urgency in the field.
The Hindu questioned India's selection, noting that Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja were left out. Asked whether their absence was felt, Gill replied: "No, I don't think so."

The draw kept India fourth in the WTC table, but their points percentage fell from 51.52 to 50, The Indian Express reported. Gill said that if India win five of their next six Tests, "we should be in a good position to qualify". The Indian Express also reported that India would need to win all six remaining Tests to have a chance of reaching the final at The Oval next year. The Hindu wrote that a win in Christchurch would be the first condition, followed by four wins in the five-Test series against Australia.

New Zealand Cricket said on Tuesday that Tickner, 33, injured his right hamstring in training in Wellington this week. He was not in the playing eleven for the first Test. Fisher, who played his only Test against Zimbabwe last year, joins the squad.
New Zealand are already without spinner Mitchell Santner, who fractured his right hand in the one-day series against India. The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.

stories.headline: Gukesh begins world title defence against Sindarov in Geneva
stories.dek: The 20-year-old champion, ranked 26th, faces fellow 20-year-old Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, ranked fourth, in the youngest world championship match on record.
stories.summary: Defending champion D. Gukesh opens his world title defence against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on Tuesday. Gukesh is ranked 26th and Sindarov fourth, making the Indian the underdog in a 14-game match.
body: Defending world champion D. Gukesh begins his title defence against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on Tuesday, with the first of up to 14 classical games set for the Fondation Martin Bodmer library in Cologny.

Both players are 20. The Hindu calculated their combined age at about 41.5 years, nine years below the previous youngest pairing, Gukesh and Ding Liren in 2024. Sindarov is roughly six months older, according to The Guardian.

Gukesh is ranked 26th by FIDE and 28th on live ratings with 2710 Elo points. The Hindu reported that this makes him the lowest-ranked reigning champion to defend the title since FIDE began publishing official ratings in 1971. Sindarov is fourth with 2782.

Gukesh peaked at 2794 in October 2024. His rating fell to 2703 in the August and September 2026 lists before he scored 8.5/11 on the fourth board at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand in September, winning a silver medal.

Sindarov won the Candidates tournament in Cyprus, finishing unbeaten with 10 points from 14 games. He also won the 2025 FIDE World Cup in Goa, The Guardian reported. He is the first Uzbek to challenge for the world title.
At Sunday's press conference Gukesh rejected the idea that he is defending. "I'm not here to defend anything," he said, according to the Indian Express. "I'm here to win it all over again."

Sindarov said he began training seriously only last year and had learned from watching the champion. "He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end," he told reporters.

Viswanathan Anand told DW that Gukesh's loss of form was not entirely surprising. "He became the world champion (very young). So suddenly the responsibility is shifted onto you and even expectations," Anand said.

The first player to reach 7½ points wins. A 7-7 score after 14 games would go to rapid and blitz tiebreaks. The prize fund is $2.5 million. Games start at 3pm local time, 7.30pm in India, and Game 1 has Sindarov playing white. The match runs to December 12, when any tiebreaks and the closing ceremony are scheduled.
keyFacts: Game 1 is on November 24; the match runs to December 12 if tiebreaks are needed.

Magnus Carlsen, still ranked first, declined to defend the title after 2021 and rarely plays classical chess now.

stories.headline: England starts trial of AI-assisted breast cancer screening for nearly 700,000 women
stories.dek: The £10 million trial will test whether AI tools can let one specialist, rather than two, review most mammogram images, the NHS said.
stories.summary: England's NHS has launched what it calls the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, expected to involve nearly 700,000 women over three years. It will test whether AI can improve early detection and free up specialists' time.
body: England's National Health Service said on Monday it has launched the world's largest trial of AI-assisted breast cancer screening, expected to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years.

The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess whether tools assisted by artificial intelligence can improve early detection of cancer in screening. Health officials hope this would free up specialist clinicians' time. The NHS said hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset.

The AI tool will help clinicians review images from routine mammograms. The NHS said appointments will proceed as normal, with the tool used alongside specialists who check the images for cancers too small to see or feel. The trial will test whether most images could be reviewed by one specialist instead of the current two.

Women attending routine screening at 30 planned sites will be given details of the trial and take part unless they opt out. Recruitment has begun at Cambridge University Hospitals in eastern England, and more sites will open in the coming months.
The trial is led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working with NHS England.

"This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement. She cited the technology's "huge potential" and promised "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly," she said.

A study published in The Lancet in January found that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists' workloads. It analysed nearly 106,000 mammograms from Sweden's national screening programme, taken between April 2021 and early December 2022.
keyFacts: The trial is expected to involve nearly 700,000 women over three years.
It is funded at £10 million ($13 million).
Thirty screening sites are planned; recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals.

stories.background: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed each year in the UK. Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, about 2.1 million screenings annually, which the NHS estimates helps prevent around 1,300 deaths.
stories.whyItMatters: If the tools prove effective, the NHS says women could be diagnosed and start treatment sooner, and specialists' time could be freed up.

stories.headline: NASA seeks industry partners to design Lunar Reactor-1, a nuclear power plant for the Moon
stories.dek: The agency wants a launch-ready 20-kilowatt fission system by 2030 that can run on the lunar surface for at least five years.
stories.summary: NASA has issued a request for proposals for industry partners to develop and test Lunar Reactor-1, a fission power system for the Moon. Proposals are due by December 21, and the agency wants a launch-ready system by 2030.
body: NASA has asked industry to propose designs for Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1), a small fission power system intended to supply electricity on the Moon, with proposals due by December 21.

The reactor would generate 20 kilowatts, which NASA said is enough to power about 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. The agency said the power could support habitats, communications systems, rovers and scientific instruments at a planned Moon Base.

NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and to operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. The solicitation requires the reactor to meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations.

Unlike solar power, a reactor can generate electricity continuously, including through lunar nights that last about 14 Earth days, NASA said. That would help in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable.

"This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface," said Brian Giblin, NASA's Lunar Reactor-1 program manager.

The Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback from a draft released in August and an industry day held in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The main purpose is to advance the technology, testing and flight design of LR-1. NASA may also issue additional task orders for other space nuclear power systems.

LR-1 is managed by NASA's Space Reactors Division in partnership with the DOE. The same division is responsible for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, scheduled to launch in 2028. That mission will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, in which a reactor's electricity powers a spacecraft's propulsion.
keyFacts: LR-1 would generate 20 kilowatts of electricity.
NASA wants a launch-ready system by 2030 and at least five years of lunar operation.

The reactor must meet Department of Energy safety standards for nuclear operations.

stories.background: NASA said lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months, and solar power becomes less effective farther from the Sun. The agency released a draft proposal in August and held an industry day in September before issuing the final request.
stories.whyItMatters: NASA says continuous power is needed for sustained operations on the Moon, including during lunar nights and in places without sunlight. The agency also links the technology to later exploration of Mars.
